items.stem: What should a data strategy be anchored to first?

options.text: The organisation's business goals and the value they require
options.rationale: Correct: data strategy exists to serve business objectives.
Technology follows strategy, not the reverse.

options.text: The preferences of the largest vendor
options.rationale: Vendor preference is not a strategic anchor.

options.text: The number of dashboards the company can build
options.rationale: Dashboard count is an activity metric, not a goal.

items.explanation: Correct: data strategy exists to serve business objectives.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO reflect good data governance for a leader? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Governance enables safe access, not only restriction
options.rationale: Correct: good governance balances enablement with control.

options.text: Sensitive data gets controls proportional to its risk
options.rationale: Correct: risk-based controls match protection to sensitivity.

options.text: All data is locked down equally regardless of sensitivity
options.rationale: Uniform lockdown blocks value and ignores risk differences.

options.text: Outcomes are measured only by number of policies written
options.rationale: Policy count is not an outcome measure.

items.explanation: Correct: good governance balances enablement with control.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: An organisation with no reliable data foundations wants to launch advanced AI immediately. What is the sound advice?

options.text: Build the data foundations first; sequence the roadmap realistically
options.rationale: Correct: advanced initiatives depend on mature foundations.

options.text: Skip foundations and deploy AI now
options.rationale: Advanced work on weak foundations tends to fail.
Roadmaps must fit the organisation's own maturity.

items.explanation: Correct: advanced initiatives depend on mature foundations.
